meta.title: Precision housings in 2027: keep buying, de-risk the supply, and hold a leased cell as a gated fallback
meta.subtitle: Answer to: make precision housings in-house in 2027, lease a flexible cell, or keep buying? For decision at the January 2027 Executive Committee
meta.purpose: Should Meridian Motion manufacture precision housings in-house in 2027, lease a flexible cell, or continue buying from an external supplier?
meta.confidentiality: Based solely on the internal briefing pack; nominal, pre-tax, undiscounted unless stated. Briefing data is synthetic

inputs.label: Finished analysis deck, extracted slide by slide

storyline.governing_thought: Keep buying in 2027 on a de-risked supply, pre-qualify a gated lease, and build no cell in 2027

exec_summary.text: Judged on four tests, not unit price, only buying with a de-risked supply fails none

sub_points.text: Our starting hypothesis, a leased cell, failed three of the five conditions it needed

exec_summary.text: The owned cell is not a 2027 option

sub_points.text: It needs $7.3M against the $5.0M capital limit and leaves ~$3.2M of cash, below the $4.0M floor
The circulated $27 saving is $16 per good housing in 2027; payback is 3.7 years at 100k units (7.2 at 65k)

exec_summary.text: Leasing is a cost near-tie that turns negative if any one assumption slips

sub_points.text: It saves $0.3M (1%) over 2027–29 in the plan, but costs $1.4M more on conservative demand
It costs $0.5M more if it runs 7 months of 2027 on full fixed cost; break-even is 207k units in 2028–29

exec_summary.text: Delivery reliability is a supply-design problem that buying can fix faster than any cell

sub_points.text: The 0.2-percentage-point shortfall (96.8% on time against 97%) traces to one flood closure
Four supply levers act in 0–13 weeks, against 5–9+ months for a cell, for $0.25M capital and ≤ $0.72M working capital

exec_summary.text: Pre-agreed gates would switch to the lease; act before the March 2027 quote expiry

sub_points.text: Triggers: committed 2028–29 volume of 208k+, a price above ~$84 (~$74 with committed volume) or on-time delivery under 97% for two quarters
The plan keeps 2027 year-end cash near $8.2M, enough to fund the lease if a gate trips

units.text: Continue buying in 2027; convert the single supplier into a dual-sourced, capacity-reserved supply with a five-layer outage contingency; pre-qualify a leased cell triggered only by pre-agreed gates; do not build the owned cell
The decision must pass four tests (affordability, like-for-like cost, delivery reliability, robustness), not a unit-price comparison
Terms as quoted for buy, lease and own: unit cost per good unit, upfront cash, fixed cost, scrap, capacity, timing, after 2029
The customer mandates reliability and dimensional quality, not insourcing; volumes are not guaranteed (conservative 2028 = 65k)
Starting hypothesis (lease) failed three of five conditions (1, 3, 4 not supported; 2 supported; 5 unproven); answer revised to buy and de-risk
Buy + de-risk is the only option with no failing test; lease fails robustness (partial on cost and reliability); owned cell fails all four
Owned cell needs $7.3M against the $5.0M limit and leaves ~$3.2M of year-end cash, below the $4.0M floor
The circulated $27 saving is $16 (15.63) per good housing in 2027; payback 3.7 years at 100k, 7.2 at 65k, not under three
Undiscounted, pre-tax; cumulative 2027–29 owned-cell savings ($5.7M) do not recover $7.3M
Even financed, the owned cell cannot help 2027 (nine-month lead time, first output ~Q4 2027); cash drops to $1.9M on payment; demo yield excludes start-up, rework, downtime
Lease saves $0.3M (1%) over 2027–29 in the plan; costs $1.4M more in the conservative case
Owned cell costs $1.6M more in the plan and $3.5M conservative; wins only if the non-binding $2.1M resale is realised
The gap is small because scrap lifts the lease's $49 to $51–52 per good unit and $1.6M a year of fixed cost absorbs the margin until ~67k a year
Lease edge vanishes with 6% lower volume, a seven-month 2027 (full-year fixed cost), or a ~$1.40 lower supplier price; break-evens 207k units, $73.6, $84.2
A 1% edge does not pay for first-time operating risk in a cell Meridian has never run
Reliability gap is 0.2 percentage points (96.8% against 97%) and traces to one flood closure
Supply levers act in 0–13 weeks; cells take 5–9+ months; any cell is a 2028 capacity decision, not a 2027 reliability fix
The machine-shop correlation is confounded and not causal; do not rely on it
Five-layer contingency (buffer, second source, reserved capacity, emergency supplier, lease fallback) for $0.25M capital and up to $0.72M working capital
Insurance arithmetic: one emergency month ~$0.1M; the lease's $1.4M downside buys ~14 months, so the contingency is cheaper unless an outage exceeds a year
Recommendation uses $0.25M of the $5.0M limit (5%), keeps year-end cash ~$8.2M ($4.2M headroom), $2.2M headroom even if the lease is triggered
Main cost exposure: $0.22M extra for each $1 the supplier adds to the 2028–29 price
Prerequisites P1 site ready, P2 spec frozen, P3 ≥94% first-year yield at full speed must all pass before a lease is signed
Triggers: T1 committed 2028–29 volume ≥208k; T2 price >$84, or >$74 with T1; T3 OTD <97% for two quarters or supplier refuses split orders/reservation; reviewed quarterly from June 2027
Owned cell: revisit no earlier than 2028 and only with $7.3M financing, committed demand ≥120k a year, ≤4% scrap proven, binding resale; decide ≥12 months ahead
Act before the March 2027 quote expiry: supply terms, second source, outage cover, lease option, governance workstreams with proposed owners
Decision requested: approve buy and de-risk for 2027, $0.25M tooling, up to $0.72M buffer, the site survey and the gates
The answer is most exposed to supplier pricing after March 2027 and to executing the contingency on time
Other uncertainties: demand above/below plan, alternate-shop price, carrying cost (~$0.5M at 25%), designation loss unquantified, nominal basis
Cost model by option, year and demand case with inputs and worked examples
Logged modelling choices mostly tilt toward the cells; † items need management confirmation
Five circulating management claims do not survive a like-for-like test
All figures nominal, pre-tax and undiscounted; briefing data is synthetic
